intro.devnet: The hackathon beta runs on Solana devnet with every feature below switched on. Each badge says what is running on this site today.
intro.mainnet: This site runs on Solana mainnet with real USDC. Each badge says what is running on this site today.
intro.mainnetIncomplete: This site is set to Solana mainnet, but the deployment is not fully set up yet, so the features below are switched off for now. Nothing runs with real USDC until the setup is complete.

settlement.title: The hammer is the payment
settlement.lead: When you win, one transaction pays the seller in USDC and moves the card to your wallet. All or nothing.

steps.title: Bid
steps.body: Place a binding bid. Nothing moves yet.

steps.title: Win
steps.body: The server clock ends the lot. The top bid at or above the minimum price wins.

steps.title: Pay
steps.body: You and the seller confirm one payment. We hold neither the money nor the card.

settlement.limits: Both sides must confirm in the payment window, or the lot shows as not completed and nothing moves. In the house room our server signs for the seller, so you confirm once.

verify.title: Check every sale yourself
verify.lead: Each paid lot has an audit page that recomputes the signed bids in your browser and reads the payment from the Solana network.

steps.title: Sign
steps.body: A key the wallet authorised for this show signs each bid. The page checks every signature.

steps.title: Hash
steps.body: Your browser hashes the signed bid log with SHA-256.

steps.title: Compare
steps.body: The page reads the payment's memo from the network and compares both hashes.

verify.limits: A matching hash shows that the log was not changed after the sale. It cannot show that no bid was left out, which is why every bidder keeps a signed copy of their own bids.

random.title: Provably fair order and randomness
random.lead: The order of the lots in the house room is drawn with a public random proof (ECVRF) that anyone can recompute.

steps.title: Commit
steps.body: Before the draw, a fingerprint (hash) of the lot list is written to the chain in a memo, so the list is fixed.

steps.title: Seed
steps.body: A block that did not exist at commit time supplies the random seed.

steps.title: Prove
steps.body: The key proves the result, and your browser recomputes the order from the proof.

random.limits: Used for the lot order and a thank-you draw, never for bids. If a draw is not finished in time, the catalogue order applies.
random.cta: See it in the house room

timed.title: Timed auctions
timed.lead: A card can stay open for hours or days instead of minutes, and it closes by itself at its deadline.

steps.title: List
steps.body: Pick a duration from 1 hour to 7 days. Bidders come back whenever they like.

steps.title: Soft close
steps.body: A bid near the end extends the clock by a few minutes, up to a cap.

steps.title: Settle
steps.body: At the deadline the top bid wins and has a longer window to pay than a live lot.

timed.limits: For now only the house and the wallets the operator allows can list a timed auction.

room.title: Demo rooms, live and timed
room.lead: The house runs one live demo room and timed demo lots, all labelled Demo. The live room starts when someone opens it, so you can watch a real auction at any hour. Every other room is made by a seller with a wallet.

steps.title: Watch
steps.body: Each lot runs on a live clock. You need no wallet to look.

steps.title: Bid
steps.body: Connect a wallet and place a binding bid.

steps.title: Spot the bots
steps.body: When the operator switches them on, house bidders appear, labelled as bots. They never outbid a person.

room.limits: It is marked DEMO: the cards are replicas owned by the platform, and after a win, a payment or an outbid the room says what a real room would have done. If a house bot wins, nothing is sold and nobody pays. To try the seller side, create your own room in the sell flow with a second wallet.

chat.title: Pre-moderated chat
chat.lead: Signed-in bidders can write in the room, and the room operator publishes each message before anyone else sees it.

steps.title: Write
steps.body: Send a short message. Only you see it, marked as waiting for approval.

steps.title: Review
steps.body: The operator approves, rejects, mutes or blocks. Links and contact details are refused.

steps.title: Publish
steps.body: Approved messages show a bidding number, never a wallet. Bots never post.

chat.limits: The filters are rules, not understanding, so a person reviews every message, and the room operator sees a popup for each waiting message. Visitors can report a message.

ai.title: AI listing agent and assistant
ai.lead: AI drafts a listing for the seller to review, an assistant picks the matching answer from our FAQ, and an agent on the AI page finds open lots and prepares a bid for you to confirm. All of it is labelled AI.

steps.title: Draft
steps.body: A seller asks for a title and a German and English text. 1 USDC buys 10 drafts.

steps.title: Review
steps.body: The draft is labelled AI. The seller edits it and ticks that they reviewed it.

steps.title: Ask
steps.body: The agent on the AI page finds open lots and prepares a bid. In a room, the assistant answers from the FAQ.

ai.limits: Every AI function needs a signed-in wallet. The agent never places a bid: you confirm and sign in the room with your own wallet. The assistant writes no answers of its own and gives no legal or financial advice. The model is Google Gemini.
ai.more: How AI is used on Hammerprice

packs.title: Packs: pay first, proof after
packs.lead: A pack is a draw from a pool of cards, with the pool and the odds public before you buy. In a chance pack you pay the pack operator directly and first.

steps.title: Pay first
steps.body: You pay the operator directly. Nothing is drawn or shown before your payment is final.

steps.title: Draw
steps.body: A public ECVRF draw picks your card, using your payment and a later block. You can recompute it.

steps.title: Deliver
steps.body: The operator signs the delivery within a deadline, or gets a strike and the pack is paused.

packs.limits: 18+ only, with a daily limit per wallet. In a chance pack Hammerprice never receives your payment (it takes only its fee in the same payment), so it holds neither your money nor the cards. For the same reason it cannot refund you if the operator does not deliver: check the operator's public delivery record before you pay. The demo pack is operated by Hammerprice itself and holds replica cards; a copy of the card you draw there is minted into your wallet.

video.title: Optional live video
video.lead: A show can carry a live camera. It is off by default, and you load the picture with one click.

steps.title: Switch on
steps.body: The seller ticks Live video under Advanced options when creating the show.

steps.title: Send
steps.body: A broadcast page sends the camera. Only wallets the platform allows may send.

steps.title: Click to load
steps.body: Your browser contacts the video server only after you press Load live video.

video.limits: The picture can lag, and the server clock decides, not the camera.

telegram.title: Telegram notifications
telegram.lead: A Telegram bot, @hammerpricebot, that tells you when you are outbid, when you win and when a payment is due, watches a live room for you and sends bid links that pre-fill a bid.

steps.title: Connect
steps.body: You press Connect Telegram while signed in. No phone number is needed.

steps.title: Tap Start
steps.body: Telegram opens the bot, and one tap links your chat to your wallet.

steps.title: Choose
steps.body: Pick your messages. /watch alerts you to a room's next lots with a bid link, and /stop ends it all.

telegram.limits: Opt-in only, and only after you link your chat. The bot never bids for you: a bid link only fills in the confirmation, and you sign in your own wallet.

wallets.title: Your wallet, your keys
wallets.lead: In auctions and equal-value packs Hammerprice never holds your USDC or your card, and it has no key that can move either.

steps.title: Connect
steps.body: Use Phantom, Solflare or Backpack. Signing in is a free signature, not a transaction.

steps.title: Bid
steps.body: A bid is a signed message that names the show, the lot, the amount and the network.

steps.title: Confirm
steps.body: Each payment needs your own confirmation. Our key only pays the network fee.

wallets.limits: On a phone, open this site inside your wallet app's own browser.
